preview: Detailed interview experience for Graduate Technical Analyst at Deutsche Bank by Nikitesh Nandale, covering online assessment, multiple technical rounds, professional fitness, and HR rounds.
content: Deutsche Bank – FTE Experience 2023-2024 Placements Nikitesh Nandale Final Year Information Technology Deutsche Bank visited our campus in first week of August to hire final year students for the role of Graduate Technical Analyst in Technology Data and Innovation (TDI) Business Division. Their criteria was: CPI : 7 and above, Branches eligible: Computers, IT & EXTC (Electronics and Telecommunication). Online Coding Round (1.5 hrs) It was an online test on HackerEarth platform. There were 3 coding questions in this round. The questions were of easy-medium difficulty. The scores for questions were 20,50,50 respectively. There were marks for partial test cases. I don’t actually remember those questions, but they were ranging from Leetcode easy to medium. You can easily find those coding questions in the experience of other students. I was able to pass all the test cases in all questions, just missed a single test case in first question. Note- Time that you take to complete your test and your current CPI matters a lot while getting shortlisted for interviews. This fact is personally witnessed by me, that’s why I am sharing this with you. So, from beginning of your first year, try to keep your CPI at least above 8+, so that you don’t have to worry about getting shortlisted. Once you are shortlisted, it becomes very easy to get the offer if you have enough preparation and decent communication skills. So, moving back to the interview experience again 40 students were shortlisted for offline interviews, which were scheduled in TPO interview cabins. Technical Interview 1 1) Implement copy constructor-> write code on paper 2) Difference between Java and C++ 3) Abstract class v/s Interface in Java 4) How will you store the image in Database using spring boot and REST Api? -> This question was resume based 5)What is Os? What is the central component of Os? what is the functionality of that component? (Ans is Kernel) 6) What is scope variable? Tell about other types of variable you know? (Ans- Instance Variable and Local variables) 7) Shallow Copy Vs Deep copy 8) He gave me two basic tables and asked to extract the given data using left join in Sql query. The tables were containing typical attributes and one common attribute was present in both of the tables. It was a standard left join SQL query. 9) He asked a standard DSA question. Delete the node from doubly Linked List. (Don’t forget to handle the edge test case here. That is deleting the head node, for this we have to append a dummy node at the start of the linked list) 10) Pattern Question Given n=5, then the code should print this inverted triangle pattern that is displayed above. He asked me to write the whole code on paper. 11) Any plans for higher studies? 12) Any questions to interviewer? (I asked him how projects and teams are allotted to new joiners) Note- I also asked him about my feedback of the interview (like how was my communication, where can I improve), he replied it was good. But later when I asked this same question to the interviewer in Professional Fitness Round, he told me that asking such type of questions are unethical. So please refrain from asking such type of questions. Technical Round 2 1)Detect the cycle in Linked List, then the code for removing the cycle 2) Difference between Linear and Non Linear Data structure 3) Construct Binary Tree from given PreOrder and Inorder traversal. 4) What is normalization? Explain all it’s types In this question , she was expecting me to know 4 NF and 5 NF also, but I smiled and said that it is not famously asked and that’s why I don’t know it. She also smiled after hearing this 5) Behavioural Question-> If you are team leader and there is a bug in the code, and it is ignored by everyone. You get know this thing one day before the deployment, then what will you do? 6) How did you execute authentication in your application. Explain all the steps. (This question was resume based) => Your answer should be very clear in such type of questions. They expect you to know everything about your project. If you get stuck in answering such type of questions then you are done). 7) A puzzle which was very confusing that I don't even remember. Obviously I was not able to answer this, and directly told her that I am not good in solving puzzles. She explained me the question three times, but I didn't get it. At last she smiled and said leave it. It’s ok if you are not able to answer puzzle questions. As many of the students were not able to answer. But solving such puzzles on the spot in an interview shows that you have good analytical skills. You can refer GFG for practicing puzzle questions. 8) What is deadlock? (don’t forget to give a real life example here) 9) How data consistency is maintained in Transactions in DBMS? (Ans- With the help of ACID properties and mainly due to Isolation property) 10) Any questions to interviewer? (I asked her how is her experience in DB so far?) Professional Fitness Round 1) What does your father do? 2) Why didn't you get a good on campus internship? 3) Tell me about the professor whom you hate the most? What is the reason of hate? 4) In which tech stack, would you like you like to work in future? 5) What are your plans regarding higher studies? 6) What work you did in your internship? 7) What difficulties you faced during the internship and how did you tackle them? 8) DSA Question => Given a string, find the LONGEST PALINDROMIC SUBSTRING out of that string. Write the code on paper, without discussing the approach in 7 minutes only. (I challenged him that I will do it in 5 minutes only, and he smiled and said go ahead) 9) Who is the president of India? 10) What was the highest score achieved by Sachin Tendulkar in 2003? (I was not able to answer this) 11) Then he asked which sport do you like and some questions related to them? 11) Any questions for me? (I asked him How is his experience in DB so far) HR Round 1) What is your native place? 2) What is your father's profession? 3) As I said in previous question that my father is in Army. So he asked why didn't I try to join Army? 4) What work you did in your internship? 5) As my internship was completely remote. So he asked what will I prefer, working onsite or remote? 6) What were the difficulties faced during internship? How did you tackle them? 7) If your manager is rude and don't respect you, then what will you do in such situation? 8) In which tech stack you would like to work? 9) If you are allowed to change the UI of WhatsApp, then what changes will you do? 10) What are the memories that you have made in college? 11) Any plan for higher studies? 12) Tell me about your journey after 10th class. 13) Any question to me? (I asked him how projects and teams are allotted to new joiners) And after this all my interviews were concluded, and we were waiting for the results in TPO Seminar hall. My HR interview ended at 7.30 pm, and still there were 2 students remaining for HR interview. So after 8.30 pm, one official from Deutsche Bank came and told us that the results will be announced in 10 minutes. The evaluation process of Deutsche Bank is very structured. Basically, marks of all the students who clear all the four rounds are calculated and then it is arranged in descending sorted order. Then the number of students that are required are selected. And I am very happy and proud to tell you that I was also one among all those 29 selected candidates. Things to avoid during preparation- 1) Everyone prepares the same thing that is DSA, OS, OOPs, DBMS, projects. But the main thing that creates difference is shortlisting. See if you don’t get shortlisted for the company then you don’t get the chance to showcase your knowledge and skills to interviewer. So make sure you get shortlisted for the company you want by maintaining a decent CPI (8+ or 7.5+) and completing the test in minimum time possible. 2) Another main thing is to keep clarity of concepts. Don’t mug up. It will not help, as interviewers will ask the questions in twisted format where your concepts will be tested. 3) Don’t give your entire time in solving DSA questions. You can solve 350 or 400 standard questions from Striver’s SDE Sheet(180 questions) and 450 Love Babbar sheet. It is more than enough to crack on campus interviews. I myself invested my entire second year in solving those DSA questions, because of this I was not having good projects in my resume in Third year. And due to this I got rejected in final round of BNY Mellon during internship drive. I got this learning from that rejection, and don’t want you to do this same mistake. So please make some good projects, so that you can mention them in your resume. It really increases the chance of getting the offer. 4) Make your communication effective. Try to explain concepts to your friends and see how much effectively you can communicate. Because without this you are not a good fit for corporate. 5) You will get all other general tips like how to explain DSA solutions in an interview, how to explain project, how to give introduction, etc from other interview experiences and from the seniors experiences(of year 2021, 2022). I am here to throw light on the reality that you will face while appearing for on campus internships and placements. 6) I myself was not able to grab a decent on campus internship and got all those learning because of this fact only. So be an all rounded personality, prepare everything like (Projects, DSA, OOPs, OS, DBMS, System Design) in depth. And lastly don’t forget to enjoy while doing preparation. Resources OOPS, OS, DBMS -> Prepare all topics from Love Babbars whimsical cheatsheet. System Design -> Shreyansh Jain playlist for High Level and Low Level both, Gaurav Sen playlist for High Level design, Sudo Code playlist on Youtube for learning additional concepts. If an average student like me can do this, then you can definitely do it. Believe Yourself and keep faith in god. All the very Best!!!!
